simple.meaning: נִאֻף (niʼuph) is a Hebrew word meaning “adultery.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: נִאֻף (H5004) appears 2 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Jeremiah 13:27, with occurrences in Jeremiah, Ezekiel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to נִאֻף (H5004) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in נִאֻף (H5004) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: נִאֻף (niʼuph) / H5004 is traced through Jeremiah 13:27, Ezekiel 23:43 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.full: H5004. niuph [ נִאֻף ] noun [masculine] adultery ; — only plural נִאֻפִים Ezek 23:43 (but ᵑ6 ᵐ5 Co נִאֲפוּ , compare Berthol); suffix נִאֻפַ֫יִךְ Jer 13:27 (Kö i. 151 ); figurative of idolatrous worship.

occurrences.englishText: I have seen your abominations, even your adulteries,
Then I said of her who was old in adulteries, ‘Now they will play the prostitute with her, and she with them.’
